N10 1.1.title: Explain concepts related to the OSI reference model

N10 1.4.title: Explain common networking ports, protocols, services and traffic types

glossary.meaning: A link-state routing protocol used inside an organisation's network.
A counter in each packet that drops by one at every router, so packets can't loop forever.

questions.q: Which OSI layer do routers mainly work at?
questions.e: Routers forward packets using IP addresses, which belong to Layer 3.

questions.q: Which OSI layer do switches mainly work at?
questions.e: Switches forward frames using MAC addresses, which belong to Layer 2.

questions.q: Which port does HTTPS use by default?
DNS uses UDP port 53 for most lookups.
questions.e: DNS mostly uses UDP 53, and TCP 53 for zone transfers and large responses.

questions.q: A network admin wants routers to share routes automatically and pick the fastest path inside the company network. Which protocol fits?
questions.e: OSPF is a link-state routing protocol for internal networks.

questions.q: What does a router do with a packet whose TTL reaches zero?
o: Sends it back to the sender unchanged
questions.e: TTL stops packets looping forever. The router usually sends an ICMP 'time exceeded' message back.
